summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a man with multiple myeloma, stage V chronic kidney disease on hemodialysis, hemolytic anemia, and type 2 diabetes, was admitted with fever, lethargy, and urinary incontinence. He was diagnosed with a urinary tract infection based on urinalysis showing white blood cells and bacteria, despite negative and contaminated urine cultures. He was treated with a seven-day course of IV cefepime and received two units of packed red blood cells for symptomatic anemia. Conjunctivitis was treated with a five-day course of topical erythromycin. His pomalidomide was held during infection and resumed at discharge. He completed dialysis during admission and was stabilized medically. He improved clinically, with resolution of fever and mental status changes, and was discharged to extended care rehab with plans for follow-up on blood counts, electrolytes, and oncology care.
